Hi Samir / Laura,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really helpful to hear about the Acme Health use case and the constraints you called out. Quick recap + suggested next steps: 

What we heard
- Goal: Real-time clinical note summarization for telehealth sessions (partial outputs shown to clinicians).
- Data: ~120k de-identified encounter notes (mix of long transcripts and short summaries). Some PHI elements remain in the raw stream before de-id.
- Primary eval priorities: coherence/faithfulness and safe redaction. Latency SLO for streaming UI: ~300ms median per chunk; tail matters.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm whether you can share a small (10-20) de-identified sample for a model-fit eval.
2) We'll run a model-fit eval focused on coherence & hallucination metrics and share the prompt set we used.
3) Follow-up call: 30 min (model-fit review + streaming UX tuning). Jordan/SE suggested to join — proposed slots next week.

Attached: Acme Health MPA (redacted) and our suggested prompt set for initial eval.

If that looks right I'll schedule the model-fit run and loop in Jordan/Alex for streaming behavior tuning.

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications before you run anything: 

- Data sharing: we can provide a de-identified sample (I'll send legal-approved files next week). Some notes still include tokenized PHI placeholders; we need to ensure redaction checks in the pipeline.
- Compliance: can you send SOC 2 evidence / quick checklist for private deployment? Procurement will ask.
- Latency: 300ms median is our target for a responsive UI, but anything under ~500ms is acceptable if coherence improves.

Also: can you recommend an initial set of models to compare? We care more about hallucination/coherence than the last 1-2% of throughput. On streaming, stop-sequence behavior is critical — partial outputs that end mid-sentence confuse clinicians.

Appreciate it — Samir

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: model fit & streaming UX — recommended models + eval plan

Hi Samir,

Appreciate the priorities — forwarded to SE/engineering. For the initial model-fit eval I recommend we compare three variants: 

- redwood-chat-xl (our curated higher-quality hosted variant) — prioritize coherence/faithfulness
- open-7b-q4f (quantized) — good cost/perf tradeoff, may show small regressions on longer context
- redwood-lite-3b (low-latency) — to validate streaming responsiveness vs quality.

Planned evals
- Prompt sets: attached eval_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (includes hallucination checks, entity-presence checks, and clinician-facing conversation snippets).
- Benchmarks: coherence (ROUGE/ENT), hallucination score (human-labeled subset), and stop-sequence correctness (automated detection of mid-sentence truncation).
- Rollout suggestion: run A/B with canary (10%) then 50/50 if results look stable. If we see quality regressions on quantized models, we can fallback to the XL variant per-request.

Related links: https://redwood.app/evals/RDW-3421 — I've created a skeleton eval run for you to review.

Next step: Jordan/Alex — can you run a quick streaming latency profile (50-200 concurrent short streams) and share results? I’ve attached the prompt set.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: streaming UX notes & latency profile (prelim)

Hi Samir / Marissa,

I ran a quick streaming-pass focused on partial output coherence and stop-sequence behavior and wanted to share high level findings plus recommended tuning knobs: 

High level findings
- Partial output coherence: When chunk flushes happen on token boundaries that align with punctuation we’re fine. The main issue is mid-word or mid-phrase flushes which create confusing partial sentences.
- Stop sequences: If the client-side stop tokens differ from the model’s stop heuristics, you can get trailing fragments.
- Latency: With redwood-chat-xl we hit ~260ms median chunk emission at our test load; quantized open-7b variants hit ~160-200ms but show an uptick in hallucination on longer contexts.

Recommended tuning
- Flush interval: 50ms with a minimum chunk size of 8 tokens (reduces mid-word flushes).
- Stop tokens: align client stop tokens to model stop heuristics (we can push a snippet).
- Prefix caching: enable short-prefix cache for repeated system instructions to reduce cold-start.
- Fallback policy: route to XL variant for requests flagged for high-fidelity (e.g., contains PHI markers).

I attached the latency profile CSV for the runs. We can adjust in the deployment config or provide a small library change on your client to align stop tokens.

If useful I can join the model-fit review and demo the streaming flow live.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: streaming_latency_profile.csv

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — technical notes on streaming behavior

Hi Samir — a few concrete technical notes from the runtime side to address the streaming UX items Jordan flagged: 

1) Chunking and flush behavior- Our runtime emits partial outputs as soon as a chunk is ready; to avoid mid-word truncation we recommend a flush policy: 
   - if (tokens_in_chunk >= 8) emit();
   - else if (time_since_last_emit >= 50ms) emit();
   - else if (token_is_eos) emit();

2) Stop sequence alignment- Ensure client stop tokens are passed to the server and validated against the model’s tokenizer. We have a small helper that maps client-side stop strings into token-aligned sequences to avoid trailing fragments.

3) Latency vs quantization trade-offs- Quantized kernels reduce latency but can increase brittle behavior on long-context hallucinations. Recommendation: run quantized as canary, instrument hallucination detectors, and auto-fallback to non-quantized on regression.

4) Instrumentation- We’ll add per-chunk headers in the streaming wire (seq-id, chunk-start, tokens-emitted, model-variant) so you can tie UI confusion to specific chunk boundaries for debugging.

Next steps
- If you share the sample de-identified notes, we’ll queue an eval and a 30-min session to walk through results.
- I’ll include the small helper for stop-token alignment in the demo repo (link shared once NDA is sorted).

Happy to jump on a call — proposed: Thu 26 Feb, 10:00 AM PST.

Best,
Alex Martinez
